purpose: The one versioned description of which parts of the QNBot glove actually provide tactile measurement, what each reading is a reading of, and which parts stay unknown. Consumers bind regions by region_id, never by array index.

evidence_classes.A: vendor-documented (protocol PDF; the pressure-layout figure is an image and was transcribed by hand, so an A geometry claim carries that residual uncertainty)
evidence_classes.B: first-party measured on this physical unit (cued press probes or recorded session bytes)

hardware.device: generic STM32 CDC device reported by the SDK as the QNBot glove; brand, model and IMU presence are only established to the extent stated below
hardware.hand_evidence: recorded session metadata declares hand=Left and the wire frame's hand_side byte is 1; the wire code is vendor-documented as 0=right, 1=left
hardware.protocol_version_note: the vendor PDF carries no version string or date; the SDK packages declare 1.2.0, which is provenance for the reading and not a wire-format guarantee

wire.checksum: little-endian uint16 at byte 546 = sum of bytes [0, 546) mod 65536
wire.checksum_kind: additive sum check, not a CRC
wire.device_timestamp_note: the frame carries no time field; ordering evidence is the (stream_sequence, frame_sequence) counter pair and time is host arrival time

grid.unit_note: the vendor documents no unit, no calibration curve and no zero definition for these cells, so a reading is a count and never a pressure or a force

mirror_rule.rule: right-hand column c corresponds to left-hand column 19 - c
mirror_rule.evidence: protocol PDF page-2 figure, two mirrored panels; transcribed by hand

finger_validity_bits.source: wire valid_mask byte at EMF relative offset 8
finger_validity_bits.rule: bit i gates the pose of finger i in the SDK order thumb..pinky; bits 5-7 are reserved with UNKNOWN meaning and are masked off, never equality-tested
finger_validity_bits.scope: gates the pose bytes of that finger, not the pressure cells of that finger

geometry.geometry_reason: the vendor DXF 手指点位示意（平面展开）.dxf was inspected read-only on 2026-10-06: 58916 lines, 854 LINE, 400 LWPOLYLINE, 17 ARC, 3 POINT, 1 MTEXT entities over 15 layers. That is an outline drawing with three isolated points, not a 460-point coordinate table, so it yields no per-taxel coordinates and no pitch. Per-taxel metric geometry therefore stays UNKNOWN and no region carries a position.

dxf_inspection.conclusion: region outlines at drawing granularity, no taxel index table, planar not a 3D surface
dxf_inspection.what_would_change_this: a vendor taxel coordinate table, or a fitted-plus-held-out measurement against known-size objects

geometry.not_a_pose_chain: the EMF finger poses are a separate channel from the pressure grid; no relation between an EMF pose and a pressure cell is documented, so this layout makes none

groups.reason: the vendor figure places the palm at rows 0-16, but this audit (declared sustained rule, 2026-10-06) measures the 340-cell block firing on 5 of 7 palm presses, on 38 of 49 finger presses and on 0 of 17 rest trials. It therefore reports that a contact exists somewhere and does not report the palm, so the identity stays vendor-only and the region stays excluded from contact
groups.also_recorded: the same audit found 3 of the recorded rest baselines stale (median absolute offset 0.0 counts): a stale baseline is what turns a whole trial into an apparent contact, and it is why this audit uses the trial's own per-cell median

regions.evidence: cued pad press 2026-09-17: 5 trials, +46..+227 counts on these bytes
cued pad press 2026-09-17: 4 trials, +71..+168 counts; only these two columns of the vendor's ring block responded
cued pad press 2026-09-17: 3 trials, +14..+116 counts; one column responded on this row

the station's bend probe measured +56 counts on these cells under a bend command; this audit's declared sustained rule finds this block firing on 3 of 13 bend-control trials and 0 of 17 rest trials, so the role is supported by two independent readings at unequal strength
vendor figure places the palm here; first-party palm press probes produced no response above the declared threshold on any of these 340 bytes

unmapped_policy.rule: every one of the 460 pressure cells that no region above covers stays class C (bytes readable, identity unknown), or D when unreadable. No cell is filled in by interpolation, by mirroring an assumption, or by a plausible-looking default, and no cell is assigned a zero position to stand for 'unknown'.

blocks.reason: distal finger rows: the vendor figure places fingers here, but no first-party press produced a response in rows 17-18
row 19 outside the index bend block
columns 12-13 of the pad rows: the vendor ring block includes them, no first-party site maps them
pinky pad row 20 beyond the single column that responded
pinky pad row 21: the probe localised three of the vendor block's four columns

unmapped_policy.coverage_rule: the layout report computes the coverage by enumerating all 460 indices; it is the authoritative count and the CLI's validate command fails on any index left in no category

probe_rounds.files: trials.jsonl plus trial-*.npz (raw frames, 548 bytes each) and baseline-*.npz (per-byte rest median)
probe_rounds.audit_reproduction: scripts/glove_tactile_bridge.py audit-regions, 2026-10-06; every trial file is hashed in the report it writes
probe_rounds.method: the trial's own per-cell median is the rest baseline; a region is responding only if its per-frame maximum stays at or above the declared threshold for at least 3 consecutive frames; the responding finger block with the largest value at that run is the attribution
probe_rounds.results: 20 of 21 pad presses attributed to the operator-named finger (the single exception is the trial whose label the station's own test records as operator-corrected), 0 of 17 rest trials showing any finger response, 0 of 7 palm presses showing a finger response, and 20 of 28 tip presses attributed (tips are reported as measured, not claimed)
probe_rounds.not_a_calibration: this establishes region identity and an ordering, never a force, a pressure or a metric position

palm_press.result: the 340-cell palm block fires on 5 of 7 palm presses, on 38 of 49 finger presses and on 0 of 17 rest trials, so it is a contact-exists indicator and not a palm indicator
palm_press.consequence: the palm stays candidate_unverified and is excluded from contact scoring

tip_press.result: 20 of 28 tip presses are attributed to the finger the operator named, and the finger blocks do not distinguish a tip press from a pad press
tip_press.consequence: the layout's granularity is per finger per pad row; no tip/pad separation is claimed

recorded_baseline_staleness.consequence: the recorded rest baselines are usable overall but not per trial, so a consumer must use the stream's own rest statistics for a region-level threshold and record which baseline it used

cross_reference.agreement: the byte groups localised there are the 50 touch cells plus the 4 index-bend cells of this layout; this layout was derived from the same raw probe trials and the two agree on which finger each group belongs to on a left hand
cross_reference.disagreement: that file records 'finger TIP presses produced almost no response on any byte'; this audit measures 20 of 28 tip presses attributed to the named finger, so the statement is not supported by the bytes and is recorded as a disagreement rather than adopted
cross_reference.note: the station config is the live station UI's own view and is not modified by this layout; the station keeps owning its own copy

calibration.reason: no first-party calibration record id exists for this unit; the vendor exposes only a factory-calibration status flag and documents no id and no data format

baseline.availability: present in a recorded session when the station captured one, otherwise a consumer must compute its own from the session's declared baseline window and say so in its output

unknowns: wire-protocol version string and whether the wire format changed across SDK versions
per-taxel metric position, taxel pitch and grid origin
pressure unit, calibration curve and zero reference
identity of rows 17-18 and of columns 12-13
whether any palm cell can ever respond
whether this physical unit's firmware matches the documented wire format (the PDF and SDK are documentation, not a device readback)
not_claimed: that a raw count is a pressure or a force
that any region's position in space is known

that the 460-cell grid is physically a regular 23x20 sensor array: the wire field is a 23x20 byte grid and the vendor figure assigns regions to it, but whether the physical sensors form a regular 23x20 array is not established
that this layout is a glove model: it carries no mesh, no joint limits and no kinematics
